key_insight: Homogeneous WC–Co–Cr powder enables dense, layered coatings, while spray method selection controls the balance between hardness and friction performance.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical machine parts, choosing between HVOF and detonation spraying lets engineers tune coating microstructure for either lower friction or higher hardness.
method: Compared WC–Co–Cr coatings made by detonation spray (DS) and HVOF.
Examined powder morphology plus coating microstructure and phase composition using SEM and EDS.
Evaluated coating performance through microhardness and tribological behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and a low friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: Reported performance depends strongly on powder quality and spray conditions, so results may not transfer directly to other feedstocks or process windows.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
